finding.claim: With cache enabled, a token with no iat claim is cached with TTL now+cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) regardless of its exp, so an expired token is still accepted from cache until that TTL elapses.
finding.source: Holder of a previously issued token that has exp but no iat (issuer signs with noTimestamp:true or otherwise omits iat). Precondition: createVerifier called with cache enabled.
finding.sink: Cache-hit acceptance in verify() at src/verifier.js:364-377 (now <= max check at line 374, where max is set in cacheSet).

trace.note: The block that reads payload.exp (lines 123-129) runs only when hasIat is true; for iat-less tokens cacheValue[2] stays 0.
cacheValue[2]===0 is replaced with maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL, so the entry outlives exp by up to cacheTTL.
Cache hit returns the cached payload when now <= max, without re-checking exp.

finding.guards_checked: exp is validated in verifyToken (verifier.js:318-322) on the first verification only. The cache TTL is the only check on later hits and ignores exp when iat is absent. Overrun is bounded by cacheTTL (default 10 min). Requires an issuer that emits iat-less tokens. Not forgery; an expiry-enforcement bypass.

finding.claim: The maxAge option is silently not enforced for tokens that lack an iat claim, because the iat validator is skipped when the claim is absent.
finding.source: Holder of an iat-less but validly signed token (issuer uses noTimestamp:true). Precondition: verifier configured with maxAge.
finding.sink: Age policy check in verifyToken validators loop at src/verifier.js:304-323 (maxAge validator registered at line 642-644).

trace.note: maxAge option pushes a validator with claim 'iat'.
if (!(claim in payload)) continue skips the validator when iat is absent.
requiredClaims is the only mechanism that would force iat to be present; it is operator opt-in and not set by maxAge.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified first (verifier.js:280). exp is still enforced if present. The maxAge check is entirely skipped for iat-less tokens, which therefore never age out under maxAge. Requires an issuer that emits iat-less tokens.

finding.claim: With cache enabled, any Buffer token throws a TypeError from hashToken before decoding, so Buffer tokens (which verify() explicitly accepts) fail with an uncaught exception instead of a TokenError.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied token passed as a Buffer (for example raw request body bytes). Precondition: cache option enabled.
finding.sink: hashToken calls token.split on a Buffer, which has no split method, at src/utils.js:46.

trace.note: Buffer tokens are accepted by the type check.
cacheKeyBuilder(token) is called with the raw Buffer.
token.split('.', 1) on a Buffer throws TypeError; this is outside any try block, so it escapes verify() synchronously even in callback mode.

finding.guards_checked: Type check at verifier.js:353 passes Buffers. Decode try/catch (386-395) is after the cache lookup and does not cover it. No Buffer-to-string conversion occurs before cacheKeyBuilder. Impact is availability and error-handling (uncaught exception, documented Buffer support broken); no auth bypass.
